Subject: Spike in hallucination rate on patient-summary promptset

Hi Vanessa / Marissa —

We're seeing a sudden increase in hallucinations from the patient-summary promptset used in our clinician workflow. The UAT monitors flagged a jump from ~0.2% to ~3.6% in the last 6 hours. I'm attaching a small sample of problematic outputs and the trace IDs. Some examples show confident but incorrect medical facts (wrong medication names/dosages).

Attachments: acme_patient_traces.jsonl (sample traces), model_metrics_q4.csv (recent metrics)

We're paused on the latest roll (it was scheduled earlier today) and need guidance on next steps — can your team advise immediate mitigations and whether this requires a rollback? Also, please confirm whether any PHI was exposed in logs.

Thanks,

Quick diagnostic summary (initial pass):
- Model variants active: model-v2-qat (rolled at 02:00 PST), fallback model-v1.8 in logs for older requests.
- Metric delta: per-turn hallucination (automated detector) increased from 0.2% -> 3.6% post-roll, confidence-weighted hallucinations jumped as well.
- Suspected root causes: quantization artifact on long-context medication lists + a recent slight prompt-normalization change that trims punctuation in multi-line notes. Both lower-level changes could increase token alignment errors for drug names.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Canary rollback: shift 100% of Acme UAT traffic back to model-v1.8 for 1 hour as a safety check. Rollback owner: Vanessa / Grace to execute; ETA 30m after decision.
2) Temporary guardrail: enable stricter hallucination filter for patient-summary route (drop or flag outputs with medical-entity mismatches). Owner: Rishi — I can push in 20m as a hotfix to the scoring layer.
3) A/B validation plan (if we want to keep v2-qat):
   - Fraction: 10% traffic to v2-qat candidate, 90% to v1.8 for 12h window.
   - Acceptance criteria: per-turn hallucination <= 0.5% absolute and no >1.0% increase in confidence-weighted FNs. Signal must be stable across 3 sampling windows (4h each).
   - Monitoring: automated alerts to Slack channel #acme-ops and Jira ACME-1245 updated with daily snapshot.

Data/privacy note: I reviewed the sample traces — no clear PHI in the dumped traces, but we should run the log-scrub job to be safe (Grace to confirm). If PHI present, escalate to Thomas from SigmaAudit (cc'ed on this thread) for remediation steps.

I'll stand by to implement the filter and coordinate the canary rollback.

—Rishi

Thanks team — clear, actionable plan. A few product-level asks before we proceed:

1) Safety-first default: I support the canary rollback (Rishi + Vanessa). If rollback shows regression gone, we keep model-v1.8 for production gates and initiate postmortem.

2) Decision window: target decision (rollback vs continue with A/B) within 1 hour of the triage call. If we choose A/B, set auto-fallback to v1.8 if the 4h rolling window crosses the acceptance thresholds.

3) Acceptance checklist for A/B success (to include in runbook):
   - Quantitative: per-turn hallucination <= 0.5% and no >0.3% increase in entity-mismatch rate vs baseline over 12h.
   - Qualitative: 30 sampled clinical summaries hand-reviewed by Acme clinical team with no high-severity errors. Acme to confirm reviewer availability.
   - Operational: rollback path validated, observability dashboards annotated, and alerting thresholds set.

4) Security/compliance: Thomas (SigmaAudit) — please confirm whether the log-scrub job meets ACME's PHI retention policy and if any extra audit evidence is required for this incident.

5) Owners & timeline:
   - Rollback execution & verification: Vanessa / Grace — 30m ETA once approved
   - Hallucination filter hotfix: Rishi — push within 20m of go-ahead
   - A/B orchestration & monitoring: Aditya — implement sampling and dashboards (if chosen)
   - Customer comms: Vanessa — provide status updates to Sara every 30m until resolved

I'll be on the triage call in 10m. Vanessa — please send the invite (include Acme and SigmaAudit).

Marissa Cole
